test_title: PYST 59: SSC MTS 2024 - English Language and Comprehension (Held On: 12 Nov, 2024 - Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Read the following sentence and select its future tense form from the options given below:

Rachel and Rahul joined forces on a project and successfully completed it within a month.

options.text: Rachel and Rahul are joining forces on a project and successfully completing it within a month.
Rachel and Rahul should join forces on a project and successfully complete it within a month.
Rachel and Rahul will join forces on a project and successfully complete it within a month.
Rachel and Rahul have joined forces on a project and successfully completed it within a month.

solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. Rachel and Rahul will join forces on a project and successfully complete it within a month.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence provided is in the past tense: "Rachel and Rahul joined forces on a project and successfully completed it within a month."
 
• The task is to convert the sentence into its future tense form.
 
• Future tense typically uses "will" followed by the base form of the verb.

Correct sentence: *Rachel and Rahul will join forces on a project and successfully complete it within a month.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Future Tense:**
 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + will + base verb.
 
• **Example:** She will visit her grandmother tomorrow.
 
• **Usage:** Describes actions or events that are expected to happen in the future.
 
 
 
• **Other Tenses:**
 
 
• **Present Continuous:** "Rachel and Rahul are joining forces..." indicates an ongoing action in the present.
 
• **Past Perfect:** "Rachel and Rahul have joined forces..." refers to actions completed before a certain point in the past.
 
• **Modal 'Should':** "Rachel and Rahul should join forces..." suggests advice or a recommendation, not a future action.
